newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Central Bank says new BOP reporting in place.
newsitem.headline: Manila Central Bank says new BOP reporting in place.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank said on Wednesday it has introduced a revised reporting system to give a better breakdown of the country's balance of payments (BOP).
The Central Bank issued the statement after an Asian Development Bank report on Tuesday pointed out large errors in the country's 1995 BOP which reached a surplus of $645 million.
"The new reporting system is designed to address the complication in BOP monitoring brought about by the liberalisation of the foreign exchange system," the Central Bank statement said.
"Such complication is not peculiar to the Philippines, but is the usual experience of countries adopting a liberal foreign exchange environment," it said.

Pilot testing of the new reporting system, which was adopted after consultations with the International Monetary Fund, started in February and was implemented, after fine tuning, since last month, the Central Bank said.
Despite the adoption of the new reporting system, the overall BOP position of the Philippines will not be revised, the Central Bank said.
The overall BOP surplus was reported at $1.8 billion for 1994 and $645 million for 1995. For the first six months of 1996, the BOP surplus reached $2.4 billion.

The Asian Development Bank report said the errors in the BOP could have arisen from the conversion of foreign currency deposits (FCD) in private banks into Philippine pesos. Double counting of receipts could have occurred as they are already taken from records of the Customs Department, it said.

The Central Bank said that before the foreign exchange liberalization in 1992, comprehensive information needed for BOP compliation could be obtained from reports submitted by commercial banks, as all foreign exchange receipts had to be exchanged for pesos to the banking system.

Such requirements had been lifted with the advent of foreign exchange liberalisation and there has been "some difficulty" in classifying the foreign currency deposits due to the lack of information on their sources and uses, the Central Bank said.
